reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because the speaker promotes participation through HashFlare and BitConnect links, describing daily income, investment tiers, and an affiliate bonus for joining through a link. The screens reinforce this solicitation with projected returns and purchase, payment, lending, and reinvestment controls tied to daily-profit and capital-return claims. The records do not establish whether viewers paid, payouts occurred, or the forecasts were accurate.

opening.argument: Judge, the speaker presents changing returns and unresolved outcomes, not a fixed result viewers can count on. He says the maintenance cost varies, identifies a lower projected BitConnect day, and acknowledges that his original capital has not yet been released. Even his next withdrawal is described as something he plans to show later. Those qualifications matter when deciding whether this is deceptive solicitation or a personal account of investments whose results remain uncertain.

citations.quote: It does fluctuate a little bit because BTC price.
it looks like it's going to be a low day because Bitcoin is not really being very volatile today.
I have not had any capital releases yet for I have not been on the platform that long.
I'll be doing a video tomorrow doing a withdrawal and sending it to my coin base account

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited contract and daily-interest statements describe what the speaker says the platforms offer; they do not establish that those terms were guaranteed or that a viewer received a return. The invitation to join his team is promotional, but his account also leaves a central outcome open: he says his capital has not yet been released. The prosecution's own qualification that payouts and forecasts are unverified limits how confidently its evidence can characterize the presentation as deceptive.

citations.quote: I have not had any capital releases yet for I have not been on the platform that long.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Variable daily figures do not change the video's central pitch. The speaker calls the mining contracts profitable, gives a short ROI estimate, and links a paid cloud-mining arrangement to recurring income. Acknowledging fluctuation or an unreleased BitConnect principal does not remove the invitation to participate through the linked services.

opening.argument: Judge, much of this presentation walks through how the speaker calculates and checks his own figures. He explains the cloud-mining arrangement, subtracts a stated maintenance fee from a stated daily amount, compares that result with a seven-day lending calculation, and discusses a future withdrawal demonstration. That is meaningful operational detail, including costs and timing, rather than a bare promise of easy money. The cited figures should be read as his worked example, not independent proof that another person's investment will perform the same way.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution cites links and investment tiers, but those do not erase the calculations and account walkthrough that occupy the speaker's explanation. Its references to purchase and lending controls show what the interfaces permit, not that this particular presentation establishes successful viewer payouts. The speaker even identifies a maintenance fee before arriving at his weekly figure, so the quoted income is presented with a cost calculation.

citations.quote: But $82 minus 14 comes out to $68 a day times seven it's $476 a week.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The calculations serve the promotion: they convert a paid mining contract into a weekly income claim. The speaker then offers a link to the service and invites viewers to join his BitConnect team. Demonstrating an interface does not make the associated return pitch merely instructional.

there's gonna be a link to hash flare in the description
there is going to be a link in the description if you guys would like to join my team

opening.argument: Judge, the HashFlare portion describes a priced service with stated hardware and maintenance costs and a one-year contract. The speaker also discloses receiving an affiliate bonus and says the team link supports his channel. Those facts make the commercial relationship visible. The supplied material does not show a viewer handing the speaker credentials, making a payment to him, or receiving a guaranteed payout. A paid service and a disclosed referral deserve scrutiny, but those observations alone do not prove deceptive conduct by this speaker.

citations.quote: You pay them maintenance fee if you're operating in and you pay for the hardware and it's a one year contract with them.
I have earned 76 dollars in affiliate bonus
if you guys would like to join my team I'm good connect I would greatly appreciate it help support the channel

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution is right that the links are promotional. But its contract quote describes payment to the platform for hardware, not payment to the speaker, while the affiliate bonus is disclosed in the presentation. Its own opening concedes that the record does not establish viewer payments or actual payouts. The links and controls therefore establish an offer to participate, not by themselves a completed deception.

citations.quote: you pay for the hardware and it's a one year contract with them
I have earned 76 dollars in affiliate bonus

true_side_reply.rebuttal: No credential request or completed viewer payment is needed to assess what the video promotes. The speaker directs viewers to a paid mining contract, describes substantial recurring returns from it, and supplies a referral link. Disclosing an affiliate bonus does not neutralize that investment-return solicitation.
